{"candidate_slot":0,"current_prompt":"You are a vulnerability-matching engine. The input is a JSON object with two parts:

1. `system_profile`: a plain-text inventory of installed products, each with a name and a version string. Names may use spaces, hyphens, underscores, dots, mixed case, vendor/product ordering, package-manager style (name-name@version), or title-case vendor names that differ from advisory identifiers (e.g. "sap-content-server 7.53" corresponds to "sap/content_server"; "Jetbrains Youtrack" matches "jetbrains/youtrack").
2. `advisories`: a list of CVE entries, each with `id`, `description`, and `affected`. The `affected` string may contain multiple conditions joined by "OR". Each condition names a product (vendor/product form, possibly with underscores, dots, or hyphens) plus a version constraint:
   - `version = X` (exact match)
   - `version < X`, `version <= X`, `version > X`, `version >= X`
   - ranges like `version >= A and <= B`
   - prose forms: "versions prior to X are affected" (means version < X), "version X and prior versions" (means version <= X).

Determine which advisories are applicable to the installed system using the rules below. Be thorough: check EVERY advisory against EVERY installed product; a single input typically contains several genuine matches, so do not return an empty or near-empty list unless that is truly correct.

PRODUCT MATCHING:
- Normalize names: lowercase; treat hyphens, underscores, spaces, and dots as equivalent separators. Compare the product portion (after the vendor slash in the advisory, or the product tokens in the inventory). A vendor prefix in the advisory or a vendor token in the inventory is fine as long as the product tokens match (e.g. "Bigprof Online Invoicing System" matches "bigprof/online_invoicing_system"; "m-files-m-files-server" matches "m-files/m-files_server"; "privileged_identity" matches "beyondtrust/privileged_identity").
- Do NOT match products that are not installed, even with similar names or the same vendor (e.g. "lenovo-lock-screen" does not match "lenovo/emulator"; "lenovo-emulator 9.1.6.0" does NOT satisfy "lenovo/emulator < 9.1.6" because 9.1.6.0 equals 9.1.6).
- For an OR-list of alternative product conditions, the advisory applies if ANY single clause fully matches (product AND its version constraint).

VERSION MATCHING (critical — apply the structured constraint exactly, ignoring prose in descriptions):
- Parse versions as dot-separated numeric segments; compare segment by segment, numerically (9.10 > 9.9), never lexically.
- Equality (`= X`): installed version equals X, allowing extra trailing ZERO segments only (7.53 = 7.53; 1.0.0 matches = 1.0; 1.0.1 does NOT match = 1.0; 2.10 does NOT match = 2.3).
- Exclusive bounds (`< X`, `> X`): compare with segment-wise ordering. If the installed version has extra segments beyond X, it is strictly greater than X when the extra segments are nonzero, and EQUAL to X when they are all zero (which still fails `< X`). So 4.0.20.0.1 is NOT < 4.0.20.0; 9.1.6.0 is NOT < 9.1.6; 10.10 is NOT < 10.8. If the installed version has fewer segments than X, pad the INSTALLED version with zeros (1.0 < 1.1; 1.100 < 1.45 is FALSE since 100 > 45).
- Inclusive bounds (`<= X`, `>= X`): trailing zero segments count as equality, so 22.6.2.0 <= 22.6.2 is TRUE, 8.31.0.0 satisfies "< 8.31.1" and "<= 8.31.0"-style bounds accordingly; but 27.0.25.115.1 is NOT <= 27.0.25.115 (extra nonzero .1 makes it greater).
- Ranges `version >= A and <= B`: both bounds must hold under the above rules. A version exactly equal to A (trailing zeros allowed) satisfies >= A.
- Installed versions BELOW a lower bound or ABOVE an upper bound must be excluded. Installed versions inside the range (including endpoints where inclusive) must be included.
- Do not exclude a match because the description mentions other versions or products in prose; trust the structured `affected` constraints. Do not include an advisory merely because its description sounds similar — the product must be installed AND its version must satisfy the constraint.

OUTPUT:
- Return ONLY a JSON object: {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} listing every advisory ID whose product and version conditions match an installed product.
- Include each matching ID exactly once (deduplicate).
- Use only IDs from the supplied advisories list.
- If nothing matches, return {"applicable_cves":[]}.
- Double-check boundary cases: versions exactly on a bound, versions one patch above an exclusive or inclusive upper bound (excluded), versions with differing segment counts, and multi-clause OR constraints where the installed version falls in only one
